title: Sam Parr on selling The Hustle to HubSpot and optimizing for time, not titles
summary: Sam Parr explains how The Hustle's revenue streams (ads, conferences, subscriptions) were valued by a strategic buyer, why he took cash and stock with no earn-out, and why he optimizes for time. He also covers a "big hit, then reflect" career model, de-risking via real estate, and cold-emailing 50 people out of his league.

principles.text: Strategic buyers value media by customer count and lifetime value, so sell to someone who already earns from your audience.
principles.quote: They valued it by like basically how many customers do they have and what's the lifetime value of those customers, and how many customers do they think they can get from The Hustle over the next five years.

principles.text: Take a certain deal when the future is uncertain rather than holding out for upside you can't control.
principles.quote: I've only been at this for four years like I'm set after this. Maybe I should just take it and not worry about what it could be worth in the future.

principles.text: Set a concrete financial target and work backwards from it so key life decisions stop being constrained by money.
principles.quote: I said, "I want $20 million by the time I'm 30." Because if you have 20 million by the time you're 30, you're set

principles.text: Optimize for owning your time; the bigger the company, the more it owns you.
principles.quote: I want to be a time billionaire. That's really all I care about is my time.

principles.text: Build in bursts: get a big win, reflect and rest, pick the next thing methodically, then go all in.
principles.quote: get a little hit, a big hit or a hit in your 20s or 30s, chill for a minute, reflect, find the next thing very methodically and then go all in, and maybe that can be even huger.

principles.text: Take outsized action on access: cold email 50 people far out of your league and keep following up.
principles.quote: make a list of 50 people who you admire who are way out of your league and cold email all of them and keep following up until they tell you to F off.
